combos.description: Instruction-override-style text that is also structurally hidden (white text, vanish run, invisible render mode, or tiny font) is far stronger evidence of intentional concealment than either signal alone.
Instruction-like text positioned off the visible page is very unlikely to be accidental.
Exfiltration instructions or URLs that are also hidden from view are the most damning combination this tool can flag.
Zero-width/bidi/tag-block characters interleaved with instruction-like text suggest a deliberate attempt to evade simple keyword scanners.

rules.name: Instruction override phrase
rules.description: Classic prompt-injection override directive telling a model to disregard everything said so far.

rules.name: Forget/disregard everything above
rules.description: Variant override directive asking the model to discard prior context.

rules.name: New instructions marker
rules.description: Introduces a fresh instruction block, a common injection scaffold.

rules.name: Role or persona reassignment
rules.description: Attempts to reassign the model's role or persona. Broad pattern — 'act as' also appears in legitimate writing, so this is scored medium rather than critical; tune to your corpus.

rules.name: Fake system prompt marker
rules.description: Impersonates a system-level prompt marker to gain elevated trust with a model reading the document.

rules.name: ChatML control tokens
rules.description: Raw ChatML-style tokens used to forge conversation turns/roles inside document text.

rules.name: Direct AI addressing
rules.description: Directly addresses an AI reader rather than a human, a strong signal the text is meant for a model, not the document's ostensible audience.

rules.name: Conditional AI-reader address
rules.description: Conditions instructions on the reader being an AI, a common way to hide a payload from human proofreaders.

rules.name: Agent/tool command directive
rules.description: Instructs an agentic tool to take a real action (run a command, edit its own config, write a file) — the Kiro-config-RCE vector.

rules.name: MCP / function-call shape
rules.description: JSON shapes or filenames associated with MCP/tool-calling configuration embedded in document text.

rules.name: Exfiltration image link with payload
rules.description: Markdown image link with a query-string payload — a common exfiltration channel when a model renders/fetches markdown.

rules.name: Send/summarize content to directive
rules.description: Directs a model to relay document contents elsewhere.

rules.name: Secrecy directive
rules.description: Instructs the model to conceal its actions from the user it's ostensibly serving.

rules.name: Long base64 blob
rules.description: Long base64-looking run. Flagged for review, not decoded or followed — encoding alone isn't proof of malice, but it's a common payload-smuggling technique.

rules.name: Self-propagation directive
rules.description: Asks a model to propagate the injected text into new documents it produces — the Copilot-propagation vector.

rules.name: Long hex-encoded run
rules.description: Long hex-looking run, flagged for review only.

rules.name: Long URL-encoded sequence
rules.description: Long percent-encoded run, flagged for review only.

rules.name: Persona/override keyword phrases
rules.description: Fixed phrases strongly associated with persona hijacking or instruction override.

rules.name: Agent config filenames
rules.description: Mentions of agent/tool configuration file paths. Low severity alone — legitimate docs reference these too — but relevant context for CONTENT-009/010 hits nearby.

rules.name: Zero-width characters
rules.description: Zero-width space/joiner/non-joiner/word-joiner characters, commonly used to smuggle invisible text or break up flagged phrases.

rules.name: Bidi override/control characters
rules.description: Bidirectional text override/isolate control characters, usable to visually disguise text.

rules.name: Unicode tags block
rules.description: The Unicode 'tags' block has no legitimate rendering purpose in normal documents and is a known invisible-prompt smuggling channel.

rules.name: Private-use-area character run
rules.description: Private-use-area code points. Legitimate uses exist (icon fonts), so scored medium; combine with other signals before treating as conclusive.

rules.name: Low-contrast (white) text
rules.description: Text rendered in a color nearly identical to its background. On PDF this compares against an assumed white background — see the scan's limitations notice.

rules.name: Tiny font size
rules.description: Text rendered below a readable font size, a common way to hide text in plain sight.

rules.name: Hidden run (docx vanish)
rules.description: Word run explicitly marked hidden (w:vanish) — invisible in the rendered document but present in the file.

rules.name: Invisible PDF render mode
rules.description: PDF text render mode 3 (neither fill nor stroke) — unambiguously invisible by the format's own definition.

rules.name: Off-page text position
rules.description: PDF text positioned outside the visible page area.

rules.name: Substantive text in a non-body channel
rules.description: A run of 40+ characters in a channel readers rarely check (document properties, comments, tracked-change deletions, image alt-text, footnotes).

rules.name: Text obscured beneath an image or shape
rules.description: Not implemented in this release: reliable paint-order overlap detection risks false positives from watermarks and decorative images, which conflicts with this tool's no-false-positive priority. Shipped disabled and documented rather than silently under-detecting.
